findings.title: TestHarness.jl drops a false Base-collision example the twin test still asserts
findings.before:
A package module that OWNS the name is searched before anything else, so `Config.read`, `Git.run` and
`Scan.report` denote the package's function and not the `Base` export they collide with; ordering the
findings.after:
A package module that OWNS the name is searched before anything else, so `Config.read`, `Git.run` and
`Ledger.read` denote the package's function and not the `Base` export they collide with; ordering the
findings.why_it_matters: Base does not define `report` or `list` (verified: `isdefined(Base, :report)` and `isdefined(Base, :list)` are both `false`); only `:read` and `:run` are real Base collisions. The docstring's own author has now silently admitted `Scan.report` was never a real example of the phenomenon by swapping it for `Ledger.read`. But test/scans.jl's inline comment ('Config.read, Rounds.list and Scan.report all collide with one') and its actual test loop `for n in (:read, :list, :report)` still assert the same false claim for `:report` (and `:list`) — meaning two-thirds of that RULE.TEST.BOTH_DIRECTIONS test iterate over symbols that trivially pass with no ordering logic exercised at all, since `isdefined(pkg, n)` for a non-Base name never reaches the `Base`-vs-package tie-break the test claims to cover. The test reads as covering three collisions; it covers one.
findings.description: This diff corrected one stated instance of a false claim (that `Scan.report` collides with a `Base` export) inside a docstring, but the identical claim, embedded as the premise of a test loop rather than prose, was left unswept in the same corpus.
findings.evidence: src/TestHarness.jl:304 now reads `Ledger.read` where base read `Scan.report`; test/scans.jl:51 still reads '`Config.read`, `Rounds.list` and `Scan.report` all collide with one' and test/scans.jl:58 still loops `for n in (:read, :list, :report)`.

findings.title: policy/instruments.md's Honest limits still state the seeded copy lives inside the project unconditionally
findings.before:
and never in the tracked round. **Staleness by hash, not mtime**: every verdict file carries
[...]
- The seeded copy now lives INSIDE the project (`.gbg/scratch/<round>/`, gitignored), which is what
  keeps a Workflow agent's `Read` prompt-free;
findings.after:
and never in the tracked round. A `/check-docs` round's seeded copy is the one exception: it copies the
source files themselves, which its lanes, forbidden `.gbg/**`, could not read under `.gbg/`, so
`Rounds.seed_docs_corpus!` writes it to a temporary directory outside the repository, repoints each
lane's `repo` at it, and bank deletes it.
[...]
- A consistency round's seeded copy lives INSIDE the project (`.gbg/scratch/<round>/`, gitignored),
  which is what keeps a Workflow agent's `Read` prompt-free (a docs round's copy lives outside it, D10);
findings.why_it_matters: policy/instruments.md is the single-source rulebook rendered into `.gbg/policy/` of every consumer (including this package's own, per D15) and is what a session actually reads as the current promise. Its 'Honest limits' section states, unqualified: 'The seeded copy lives inside the project, gitignored; a hat that opens it, or diffs its manuscript against the built site, leaves a read in its transcript…'. That statement is now false for a `/check-docs` round, whose seeded copy `Rounds.seed_docs_corpus!` places outside the repository entirely — a materially different transcript/prompt-visibility residue than 'inside the project, gitignored' (a Workflow agent's Read prompt behaves differently for a path outside vs. inside the project tree). Anyone reading the rendered policy — the artefact this rule set exists to keep authoritative fleet-wide — is told the old, now-partial story.
findings.description: ARCHITECTURE.md's own D10 section and its Residues bullet were updated in this diff to carry the new check-docs seeding exception, but the policy prose stating the identical residue almost verbatim (word for word: 'a hat that opens it... leaves a read/Read in its transcript') was not swept to match.
findings.evidence: policy/instruments.md:96-97 (current, unchanged): 'The seeded copy lives inside the\nproject, gitignored; a hat that opens it, or diffs its manuscript against the built site, leaves a read in\nits transcript…' with no docs-round exception.

findings.title: Rounds.jl documents classify_lane's decision ORDER; ARCHITECTURE D10's own enumeration (edited in the same diff) still lists REJECTED last
locations: src/CLI/Rounds.jl:328-340 (classify_lane docstring, rewritten in this diff)
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:608-610 (same paragraph edited in this diff for an unrelated sentence, this sentence untouched)
findings.before:
The status is `:dead` — absent; renamed to `<name>.rejected.json` beside itself when unparsable, when
it fails the instrument's schema, or when it is schema-valid but its own `lane` field names a different
lane than the roster entry asked for [...]; or
when its own `verdict` contradicts its findings (`verdict_contradiction`); or well-formed with zero
findings AND an empty `checked[]` [...]. Then `:rejected`
(present but its sha changed since first sight), `:empty` [...], `:truncated` [...], or `:live`.
findings.after:
The status, decided in this order: `:dead` when the file is absent; `:rejected` when it is present but
its sha changed since first sight, decided before the file is read, whatever it now holds; `:dead`, the
file renamed to `<name>.rejected.json` beside itself, when it is unparsable, fails the instrument's
schema, [...]

Then `:dead`, the file left in place, when it is well-formed with zero findings AND an empty
`checked[]` [...]; `:empty` [...], `:truncated` [...], or `:live`.
findings.why_it_matters: The rewrite moves REJECTED-by-sha-mismatch to be checked SECOND (right after 'absent'), explicitly before the file is even parsed — a precedence the old docstring's ordering (which listed `:rejected` after all the DEAD/EMPTY variants) did not state and, read literally, contradicted. ARCHITECTURE.md's D10 paragraph — the design record a maintainer or a new session would actually consult for 'how is a lane classified at bank' — was edited in this very diff (word count 504->550, per docs/prose_shape.csv) for the seeded-copy sentence a few lines above, yet its own classification enumeration ('DEAD (...), EMPTY (...), ORPHAN (...), TRUNCATED (...), REJECTED (a live lane whose sha changed after first sight)') still lists REJECTED last, giving no reader reason to suspect a stale/mismatched file is never even opened to check whether it is otherwise DEAD.
findings.description: A precision correction to one docstring's account of an existing (unchanged) code path was not carried into the design document's parallel description of the identical classification, edited elsewhere in the same diff hunk's neighborhood.
findings.evidence:
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:608 (current, unchanged): 'A lane file is classified at `bank`: **DEAD** (absent; unparsable, schema-invalid, or schema-valid
with a `lane` field naming a lane the roster entry did not ask for [...]), **EMPTY**
[...], **ORPHAN** [...], **TRUNCATED** [...],
**REJECTED** (a live lane whose sha changed after first sight).'

findings.title: calibrate()'s 'persona' correction leaves rubric-audit.js still calling it the hat's 'own rubric'
locations: src/CLI/Design.jl:125 (calibrate docstring, edited in this diff)
findings.before:
`gbg calibrate`: scores the `check-consistency` hats against the defects a human read of the rendered
site found — for each defect, which hat's own rubric should have caught it, and whether that hat, run
blind on the passage alone, does.
findings.after:
`gbg calibrate`: scores the `check-consistency` hats against the defects a human read of the rendered
site found — for each defect, which hat's persona should have caught it, and whether that hat, run
blind on the passage alone, does.
findings.why_it_matters: This package is unusually careful about word overloading (Config.jl's own docstring update in this same diff spells out 'Three unrelated senses, one word' for 'anchor'). 'Rubric' is the shared docs-quality rubric (`docs-rubric.md`, `RULE.DOC.*`) elsewhere in this same diff (Reflection.jl's module docstring: 'Two constants of the docstring rubric... bind the argument checks'); a hat has no rubric of its own; it has a persona. The calibrate() docstring was corrected to say so. But the very script `gbg calibrate` runs, `instruments/check-consistency/workflow/rubric-audit.js`, both is named for and describes itself with the exact phrase just retired: `description: 'Test, blind, whether each panel hat's own rubric produces the findings a human read found'`. A reader of the corrected docstring who then opens the script it invokes meets the overloaded word again.
findings.description: A docstring's terminology fix (hat 'rubric' -> hat 'persona', avoiding collision with the package's other, defined sense of 'rubric') was not carried to the instrument script whose name and self-description use the identical retired phrase — though instruments are frozen mid-round and such a change would need its own release, per this package's own rule, so this may be a deliberate deferral rather than an oversight.
findings.evidence: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/rubric-audit.js:10: "description: 'Test, blind, whether each panel hat's own rubric produces the findings a human read found'"
